subject: Agriculture
title: From Villages to Cities
description: A fast breakdown of From Villages to Cities for builders.

hook.text: Farming created food surpluses. Surpluses let some people stop farming—and start doing other things.

buildup.text: Specialists emerged: potters, weavers, priests, soldiers. None of them grew their own food.

discovery.text: Villages grew into towns, then cities. Jericho had a thousand residents by 8000 BCE.

twist.text: Surpluses also created inequality. Those who controlled the grain controlled everyone else.

climax.text: Writing itself was invented to track grain stores. The first documents were farm receipts.

punchline.text: Civilization began with a surplus of wheat.

quiz.question: What was the primary purpose of the earliest writing systems?
options: Tracking grain stores and agricultural records
